column1: Neuroscientist Jonah Lehrer considers the emotional power of music
column2: 神经科学家乔纳·莱勒探讨音乐打动人心的力量。

column1: Why does music make us feel?
column2: 音乐为什么能让我们产生情感？
column4: make us feel|使我们产生情感

column1: On the one hand, music is a purely abstract art form, devoid of language or explicit ideas.
column2: 一方面，音乐是纯粹抽象的艺术形式，既没有语言，也没有明确表达的观念。

column1: And yet, even though music says little, it still manages to touch us deeply.
column2: 可是，音乐虽少有言说，却依然能深深打动我们。
column6: touch us deeply|深深打动我们

column1: When listening to our favourite songs, our body betrays all the symptoms of emotional arousal.
column2: 听着喜爱的歌曲，我们的身体会不由自主地显露出情绪被唤起的种种迹象。

column1: The pupils in our eyes dilate, our pulse and blood pressure rise, the electrical conductance of our skin is lowered, and the cerebellum, a brain region associated with bodily movement, becomes strangely active.
column2: 瞳孔扩张，脉搏加快，血压升高，皮肤电导下降；就连与身体运动相关的小脑也变得异乎寻常地活跃。

column1: Blood is even re-directed to the muscles in our legs.
column2: 甚至连血液也会重新流向腿部肌肉。

column1: In other words, sound stirs us at our biological roots.
column2: 换言之，声音从生理的根本层面触动了我们。

column1: A recent paper in Nature Neuroscience by a research team in Montreal, Canada, marks an important step in revealing the precise underpinnings of ‘the potent pleasurable stimulus’ that is music.
column2: 加拿大蒙特利尔的研究团队最近在《自然·神经科学》发表了一篇论文。这项研究迈出了重要一步，揭示了音乐这种“强有力的愉悦刺激”背后的具体机制。
column5: marks an important step|标志着重要进展

column1: Although the study involves plenty of fancy technology, including functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and ligand-based positron emission tomography (PET) scanning, the experiment itself was rather straightforward.
column2: 这项研究用到不少先进技术，包括功能性磁共振成像（fMRI），以及基于配体的正电子发射断层扫描（PET），但实验本身相当简单。
column4: functional magnetic resonance imaging|功能性磁共振成像
column6: positron emission tomography|正电子发射断层成像

column1: After screening 217 individuals who responded to advertisements requesting people who experience ‘chills’ to instrumental music, the scientists narrowed down the subject pool to ten.
column2: 研究者刊登广告，招募听器乐时会感到“一阵颤栗”的人。在对217名应征者进行筛选后，最终选出了10名受试者。
column4: responded to advertisements|回应招募广告
column5: chills|n. 因音乐引起的颤栗感

column1: They then asked the subjects to bring in their playlist of favourite songs — virtually every genre was represented, from techno to tango — and played them the music while their brain activity was monitored.
column2: 接着，研究者请受试者带来各自最喜欢的曲目清单，几乎什么类型都有，从科技舞曲到探戈一应俱全。他们随后播放这些音乐，同时监测受试者的大脑活动。

column1: Because the scientists were combining methodologies (PET and fMRI), they were able to obtain an impressively exact and detailed portrait of music in the brain.
column2: 由于结合使用PET和fMRI这两种研究方法，科学家们得以极为精确、详尽地描绘音乐在大脑中激起的活动。
column3: combining methodologies|结合多种研究方法
column5: impressively exact|精确得令人印象深刻

column1: The first thing they discovered is that music triggers the production of dopamine — a chemical with a key role in setting people’s moods — by the neurons (nerve cells) in both the dorsal and ventral regions of the brain.
column2: 他们首先发现，音乐会引发多巴胺的产生。多巴胺是一种在调节人的情绪方面起关键作用的化学物质，产生它的是大脑背侧和腹侧区域的神经元，也就是神经细胞。
column6: setting people’s moods|调节人的情绪

column1: As these two regions have long been linked with the experience of pleasure, this finding isn’t particularly surprising.
column2: 这两个脑区长期以来就被认为与愉悦体验有关，因此这一发现并不特别令人意外。

column1: What is rather more significant is the finding that the dopamine neurons in the caudate — a region of the brain involved in learning stimulus-response associations, and in anticipating food and other ‘reward’ stimuli — were at their most active around 15 seconds before the participants’ favourite moments in the music.
column2: 更值得注意的是尾状核里的多巴胺神经元。尾状核参与学习刺激与反应之间的联系，也参与对食物及其他“奖赏”刺激的预期。在参与者最喜欢的音乐片段到来前约15秒，这些神经元的活动就达到了高峰。
column5: stimulus-response associations|刺激与反应间的联系
column8: at their most active|处于最活跃状态
column9: participants’ favourite moments|参与者最喜欢的音乐片段

column1: The researchers call this the ‘anticipatory phase’ and argue that the purpose of this activity is to help us predict the arrival of our favourite part.
column2: 研究者将此称为“预期阶段”，认为这种活动的作用是帮助我们预判最喜欢的片段何时到来。

column1: The question, of course, is what all these dopamine neurons are up to.
column2: 问题当然在于，这些多巴胺神经元究竟在做什么？

column1: Why are they so active in the period preceding the acoustic climax?
column2: 为什么在音乐的声响达到高潮之前，它们会如此活跃？
column4: period preceding|在……之前的一段时间

column1: After all, we typically associate surges of dopamine with pleasure, with the processing of actual rewards.
column2: 毕竟，我们通常把多巴胺的激增与愉悦联系在一起，也就是与处理实际获得的奖赏联系起来。

column1: And yet, this cluster of cells is most active when the ‘chills’ have yet to arrive, when the melodic pattern is still unresolved.
column2: 然而，这群细胞最为活跃时，那种“颤栗感”尚未到来，旋律的走向也还悬而未决。
column5: have yet to arrive|尚未到来

column1: One way to answer the question is to look at the music and not the neurons.
column2: 要回答这个问题，一个办法是把目光从神经元转向音乐本身。

column1: While music can often seem (at least to the outsider) like a labyrinth of intricate patterns, it turns out that the most important part of every song or symphony is when the patterns break down, when the sound becomes unpredictable.
column2: 音乐常常像一座由复杂模式组成的迷宫，至少外行人可能这么觉得。但事实证明，每首歌曲或交响曲中最重要的时刻，恰恰是这些模式被打破、声音变得难以预测的时候。
column6: it turns out that|结果表明

column1: If the music is too obvious, it is annoyingly boring, like an alarm clock.
column2: 如果音乐的走向太容易猜到，就会像闹钟声一样，单调得惹人厌烦。

column1: Numerous studies, after all, have demonstrated that dopamine neurons quickly adapt to predictable rewards.
column2: 毕竟，大量研究都已表明，多巴胺神经元很快就会适应可以预料的奖赏。

column1: If we know what’s going to happen next, then we don’t get excited.
column2: 如果知道接下来会发生什么，我们也就不会兴奋了。

column1: This is why composers often introduce a key note in the beginning of a song, spend most of the rest of the piece in the studious avoidance of the pattern, and then finally repeat it only at the end.
column2: 因此，作曲家常在一首歌开头引入一个关键音；接下来的大半首曲子里刻意避开原来的模式，直到最后才把它重现。
column4: introduce a key note|引入一个关键音

column1: The longer we are denied the pattern we expect, the greater the emotional release when the pattern returns, safe and sound.
column2: 期待中的模式迟迟不来，等待越久，等它终于安然重现时，我们感受到的情绪释放就越强烈。

column1: To demonstrate this psychological principle, the musicologist Leonard Meyer, in his classic book Emotion and Meaning in Music (1956), analysed the 5th movement of Beethoven’s String Quartet in C-sharp minor, Op. 131.
column2: 为说明这一心理原理，音乐学家伦纳德·迈耶在其经典著作《音乐的情感与意义》（1956年）中，分析了贝多芬升C小调弦乐四重奏（作品131）的第五乐章。

column1: Meyer wanted to show how music is defined by its flirtation with — but not submission to — our expectations of order.
column2: 迈耶想表明，音乐的特点就在于它不断撩拨我们对秩序的期待，却又不肯完全顺从这种期待。
column6: expectations of order|对秩序的期待

column1: Meyer dissected 50 measures (bars) of the masterpiece, showing how Beethoven begins with the clear statement of a rhythmic and harmonic pattern and then, in an ingenious tonal dance, carefully holds off repeating it.
column2: 迈耶逐一剖析这部杰作的50个小节，说明贝多芬如何先清晰地呈现一个节奏与和声的模式，然后又如何巧用调性变化，小心地把这个模式的重现一再推迟。
column6: rhythmic and harmonic pattern|节奏与和声模式

column1: What Beethoven does instead is suggest variations of the pattern.
column2: 贝多芬转而暗示了这一模式可能出现的种种变形。

column1: He wants to preserve an element of uncertainty in his music, making our brains beg for the one chord he refuses to give us.
column2: 他想在音乐中保留一点不确定性，使我们的大脑苦苦渴求他偏不肯给出的那个和弦。
column4: an element of uncertainty|一丝不确定性

column1: Beethoven saves that chord for the end.
column2: 贝多芬把那个和弦留到了最后。

column1: According to Meyer, it is the suspenseful tension of music, arising out of our unfulfilled expectations, that is the source of the music’s feeling.
column2: 迈耶认为，音乐中的情感源自悬念带来的张力，而这种张力又来自我们尚未得到满足的期待。
column5: unfulfilled expectations|尚未得到满足的期待

column1: While earlier theories of music focused on the way a sound can refer to the real world of images and experiences — its ‘connotative’ meaning — Meyer argued that the emotions we find in music come from the unfolding events of the music itself.
column2: 较早的音乐理论关注声音如何指向现实世界中的形象和经验，也就是它的“联想意义”。迈耶则认为，我们在音乐中感受到的情感，来自音乐本身逐步展开的进程。

column1: This ‘embodied meaning’ arises from the patterns the symphony invokes and then ignores.
column2: 这种“内在意义”来自交响曲先唤起、随后又置之不顾的那些模式。
column3: embodied meaning|音乐本身蕴含的意义

column1: It is this uncertainty that triggers the surge of dopamine in the caudate, as we struggle to figure out what will happen next.
column2: 正是这种不确定性，让我们在费力猜测下一步将发生什么时，尾状核中的多巴胺骤然增加。

column1: We can predict some of the notes, but we can’t predict them all, and that is what keeps us listening, waiting expectantly for our reward, for the pattern to be completed.
column2: 我们能预料其中的一些音符，却不能预料全部。正是这一点让我们一直听下去，满怀期待地等待奖赏，等待那个音乐模式最终完整呈现。
column5: keeps us listening|让我们继续听
